findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository read access can retrieve these long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which hold secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are exposed in cleartext to any principal able to read the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy would provide a separate access-control boundary.
The function uses nodejs12.x, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime unaddressed.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group or subnet-level egress controls, easing data exfiltration of the embedded credentials.

The trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so it is not scoped to the specific function or account, widening the confused-deputy surface.
